entries.description: Every tab has a new look, built to match Discord's own settings pages.
Settings are grouped into collapsible blocks that remember if they are open, with an overview of what is on at the top.
Something not working? Send your setup to the developer from the bottom of the Settings tab. Your Roblox token is never included.
Snipes are now a timeline grouped by day, colored by result. Search stays on top, and the filter and clear options moved into menus.
The details window shows the timing on top, the biome result, and what happened step by step. Switch to Raw to see the full log.
Turn Join, Notify and Forward on or off right from each trigger. Hover a button to see what it does.
The tabs are replaced by a side menu. Everything you need is in Essentials, and the optional sections show a dot when they are set up.

entries.text: Try your own messages in the match preview
entries.description: Type a message under the preview to check if your trigger would match it.

entries.text: Updates, Stats, Utilities and Developer tabs
entries.description: Cleaner layouts, with tooltips that explain each option.
New "By Server" and "By Trigger" charts show where your snipes are coming from at a glance. Hover a slice (or the legend) to see the exact count and its real/bait/timeout split.

entries.text: Right-click menu for Snipe History entries
entries.description: Quick actions on any entry: view details, jump to the message, copy the server link, join server, or remove it.
The new charts sit right below the overview cards, above the per-trigger list.
Hover a trigger to reveal a drag handle on the left and reorder by dragging. Disabled while any search or filter is active.
Replaced the right-click action on triggers with a menu with quick actions like enable/disable, duplicate, export, etc.
Reorder triggers with ▲▼ buttons instead of dragging them, for anyone who prefers it.
Disable to go back to right-click instantly toggling enabled/disabled instead of opening the context menu.
Force-kill a running macro right after joining a snipe, before it can detect the biome and send a false alert to your macro's webhook.
Pick a known macro to auto-fill its kill target (Maxstellar, FishSol, Coteab, J.JARAM, SolsScope), or choose Custom to set your own.
Confirms whether the configured process name or window title actually matches something running, before you rely on it during a live snipe.
